overall: The AG found the Westminster Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: no outside-meeting communications among a quorum regarding the solar site plan were shown, and the April 24 and Town Planner allegations were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged similar violations at the Board's April 24, 2018 meeting; the complaint was filed about two months later.
allegations.key_passage: Because this complaint was filed with the Board roughly two months later, on July 25, 2018, we find it to be untimely and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Town Planner improperly discouraged input from both the Board and the public.
allegations.key_passage: As such, he is not subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board or Town Planner secretly decided to expand the Cresticon solar project without proper Board discussion or public input before the June 26, 2018 vote.
allegations.key_passage: Based on our review, we find that the Board did not communicate with each other, or via the Town Planner, outside of a meeting regarding the Cresticon application prior to its approval of the project on June 26, 2018.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Town Planner secretly made the decision without Board input; the AG treated this as outside the law's scope.
allegations.key_passage: the law does not govern the actions of public officials who are not members of a public body, nor does it govern a public body's delegation of its authority.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
